component.name: braids
component.summary: Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix in one app

description.p: braids is an open source desktop messenger: your Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix chats in one inbox. Messages stay on your computer.

ul.li: One chat list for all accounts, with favorites, an unread filter and archive
Photos, videos, files, stickers, link previews and voice messages (record and play)
Replies, reactions, edits, mentions, forwarding, pinned messages and polls
Search across all chats, shared media, keyboard shortcuts for everything
Desktop notifications, tray icon, light and dark theme

description.p: braids is not affiliated with Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal or Matrix. WhatsApp support is unofficial; WhatsApp may restrict accounts using it.

screenshot.caption: All chats of all messengers in one inbox
Forward messages to any chat, on any messenger

ul.li: Matrix groups: add people (they get an invitation) with "Add people" in the group info, remove them from a member's menu ("Remove from group").
Hover preview: rest the pointer on a chat in the list to read its new messages (or the last ones) in full without opening it; they stay unread.
F11 toggles fullscreen (a shortcut you can change in Settings → Keyboard).
NixOS: a guide to installing braids with a system flake, in the README and linked from the website.
Sidebar: only All chats shows its unread count in color.
New group (Matrix): only people are offered as members, no longer the rooms of direct chats (!… ids that could not be added) and groups.
Settings → About → Report a bug fills in the braids version, how braids was installed, your distribution, kernel and desktop, and your messengers.
In the image viewer, Ctrl + / Ctrl − / Ctrl 0 zoomed the whole app instead of the picture.
Nix: nix run github:pebll/braids stopped with "cannot write modified lock file": the flake's lock file was missing.
Flathub: a manifest that builds braids from source, offline (utils/dist/flathub, built by the Flathub workflow), for the submission to Flathub.
Nix and NixOS: nix run github:pebll/braids runs the latest release (or nix profile install github:pebll/braids).
A new braids version is also announced as a desktop notification (once per version, with desktop notifications on), and is checked for while braids keeps running, not only at start.

Poll results: the leading option's bar is full and the others relative to it, each option shows its number of votes and the pictures of up to five voters (+N for more; Telegram does not tell who voted).

Chat list: photos, voice messages, videos and files in the last message show an icon; photos a small preview ("3 Photos" with up to three for photos sent together), voice messages their length ("Voice message (2:12)") instead of the file name.
The Flatpak is now io.github.pebll.braids (was org.braids.app), as Flathub requires.
WhatsApp: votes in polls reach the other phones.

After a start or an update, names and profile pictures show at once: braids keeps the pictures it knows (braids-avatars.json in the account's profile) and loads the saved names before the messenger's contact sync; pictures are then checked for changes in the background (they were fetched again one by one, names waited for the connection).
Polls on all messengers: see them with live results, vote (and take the vote back), make your own with the poll button next to the attach button (single or multiple choice, up to 12 options).
Text size: Settings → General, or Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Minus / Ctrl+0 (also Ctrl+=).
Emoji shortcodes: type : and a few letters (:thu) for suggestions, Tab or Enter inserts.
"Copy image" in the menu of photos.
Settings → About: Report a bug, Suggest a feature, Known issues (GitHub).
Image viewer: Show in chat, Copy image (also Ctrl+C) and Save as (also Ctrl+S) next to "Open with default app".

Matrix invites can be accepted or declined in braids: an invited room shows "<name> invited you" and Join / Decline instead of the message box (it said to use another Matrix client, and its name started with "[Invite]").
Select several messages ("Select" in the message menu, or Ctrl+click; Shift+click adds a range) to forward, copy or delete them together.
Keyboard shortcuts overview: Ctrl+/ lists all shortcuts with your own bindings, and links to Settings → Keyboard to change them.
Profile pictures open in full size: the viewer shows the small picture at once and switches to the full-resolution one when it has been fetched (Telegram, WhatsApp and Matrix; Signal has one size).
Test builds of pull requests: install.sh --pr <number> (or --branch <name>) installs them without a release; see the website's download section.
The app icon reads at small sizes (GNOME top bar, browser tab): a bigger braid with thicker strands on a warm grey circle that stays visible on dark panels.
Shortcuts follow the key's character on any layout: Ctrl+, opens Settings also where "," sits on the US M key (it went to Matrix).
The tray icon could stay empty in GNOME's top bar after braids restarted: every start reused the same icon file name, which the panel kept cached.
Labels no longer break onto two lines in narrow controls ("On top" in Settings, "Message a contact" in New chat).
"Go to" shortcuts (folders, accounts, Ctrl+N with nothing unread, back to chat list) clear the search.
Messages you send show up at once.
braids reconnects right after the computer wakes up or the network comes back, instead of waiting for the connection to time out.
Keyboard: Alt+J/K (and the arrow keys) move a highlight through the chat list and the search results without opening anything.
An "Unread" folder (Ctrl+U) with the unread chats.
An unread chat opens at the "New messages" line, a read one at the newest message.
Click a profile picture in the chat info to see it full size.
Ctrl+N with no unread chat left closes the open chat.
Videos (MP4 and others), GIF videos and video stickers play in the app.
Search the messages of all chats from the chat list (Ctrl+Space).
Stickers and GIFs show inline, including Telegram's animated stickers.
Previews for links in messages.
An emoji picker in the composer, with search and recently used emoji.
A bar for pinned messages at the top of a chat.
Create new groups on Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix.
Drag and drop files into a chat.
Ctrl+C copies text: the selection, or the message under the mouse.
The first release.
Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix (with end-to-end encryption) in one desktop app for Linux.
One chat list across all accounts, with folders for each messenger, favorites, muting, archive and "mark unread".
Text with formatting, replies, reactions, @mentions, edit and delete.
Photos and videos with a built-in viewer and player, files, and voice messages (play and record).
Forward messages from any messenger to any other.
Join groups by invite link.
Shared media for each chat, read receipts, typing indicators, notifications and an unread tray icon.
